nodes.label: AI Action Confirmation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Persistent or destructive AI-assisted actions require explicit confirmation and a tested mutation-confirmation flow.

nodes.label: Derived Search Indexes
nodes.rationale: Indexes can be rebuilt from authorized object data and metadata, but stale or degraded states must be represented explicitly to avoid misleading results or revoked-data leakage.
nodes.source_location: ### Treat search indexes as derived state

nodes.label: Evidence Classification
nodes.rationale: Observed behavior is CONFIRMED, INFERRED, UNKNOWN, or BLOCKED; only direct repeatable observation qualifies as CONFIRMED.

nodes.label: Consequential Action Safety Boundaries
nodes.rationale: Audits stop before billing, credential, OAuth, publication, invitation, or destructive actions and classify the remaining behavior as BLOCKED pending explicit authorization.

nodes.label: Reconstruction Metadata
nodes.rationale: Human-readable formats alone cannot preserve data sovereignty; full exports need a machine-readable manifest for identities, schemas, metadata, relations, attachments, and collections.

nodes.label: Protected Branch Workflow
nodes.rationale: Branch protection, required CI, squash merge, and explicit post-merge cleanup govern repository delivery.

nodes.label: Intelligent Delta Spec Merge
nodes.rationale: Apply delta intent to canonical specs while preserving main-spec content not mentioned by the change.

nodes.label: Data Portability Offline Quality Change Metadata
nodes.community_name: Data Portability Offline Quality Change Metadata

nodes.label: Globe Icon
nodes.rationale: A compact monochrome globe symbol formed by an outer circle and curved latitude and longitude bands, suitable for representing the web, world, language, or global navigation.

nodes.label: Quality Aggregate Gate
nodes.rationale: Preserve one stable branch-protection context while exposing format, lint, typecheck, test, and build failures separately.

nodes.label: Canonical Agent Configuration
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md and .agents are the sole portable repository sources for agent instructions and capabilities.

nodes.label: High-impact Human Gates
nodes.rationale: Protected workflow bypasses, merges, production operations, destructive actions, secrets, IAM, billing, tags, and force pushes require explicit authorization.

nodes.label: Unverified Deployment Trigger
nodes.rationale: CI, merges, tags, and releases must not be assumed to deploy until the Firebase App Hosting trigger is verified and documented.

nodes.label: Coverage as a Quality Signal
nodes.rationale: Coverage supports regression review without an arbitrary global threshold.

nodes.label: Deployment Automation Non-goal
nodes.rationale: Do not add deployment workflows until the App Hosting trigger and OIDC identity are verified.

nodes.label: CodeQL Security Policy
nodes.rationale: Use CodeQL as a high-signal scanner and promote its aggregate check to required only after stable code-scanning support is confirmed.

nodes.label: Next.js Wordmark
nodes.rationale: A wide black NEXT.JS typographic wordmark on a transparent background, serving as Next.js framework branding rather than an interactive UI diagram or data visualization.

nodes.label: Maintaining AGENTS.md
nodes.rationale: Agent instructions should be concise, actionable, and backed by exact repository evidence.

nodes.label: Evidence-Backed AGENTS.md Decisions
nodes.rationale: Exact external references and one canonical instruction file reduce duplication and discovery ambiguity.

nodes.label: Provenance-First Ranking
nodes.rationale: Trust outranks popularity, and compatibility does not override trust.

nodes.label: Read-Only Federated Plugin Discovery
nodes.rationale: Discovery must remain read-only and separate candidate discovery from installation or execution.

nodes.label: Object Type Schema Versioning and Migration

nodes.label: Relationship and Graph Index Freshness
nodes.source_location: Requirement: Relationship and Graph Index Freshness

nodes.label: Typed Object Domain Design
nodes.rationale: Objects, rather than files, are the durable unit of knowledge; type schemas and mutations require explicit versioning, authorization, and revision semantics.

nodes.label: Explicit and Derived Connection Design
nodes.rationale: Durable typed links and backlinks must remain visually distinct from inferred semantic suggestions, while graphs remain deterministic, accessible, and backed by explicit index states.

nodes.label: Structured Thought Surface Design
nodes.rationale: Persist deterministic valid document structure, keep metadata connected but visually distinct from prose, and treat presentation as a non-mutating view mode.

nodes.label: Risk-Proportional Completion Evidence
nodes.rationale: Completion requires task-appropriate evidence rather than an agent assertion.

nodes.label: Bounded Retry and No-Progress Detection
nodes.rationale: Repeated failures require strategy change, specialist review, blocking, or escalation rather than indefinite retries.
nodes.source_location: ### Requirement: Retries are bounded and no-progress is detected

nodes.label: High-Impact Human Gates
nodes.rationale: Protected-branch bypass, deployment, destructive operations, credentials, tags, and merges require explicit human authorization.
nodes.source_location: ### Requirement: Human gates protect high-impact actions

nodes.label: Separate Software and OpenSpec Verification
nodes.rationale: Passing software checks and validating requirements are distinct forms of completion evidence.
nodes.source_location: ### Requirement: Software verification is distinct from OpenSpec verification

nodes.label: OpenSpec Responsibility Boundary
nodes.rationale: Agent configuration references OpenSpec but must not duplicate durable requirements or lifecycle artifacts.

nodes.label: Confirmation for Persistent AI Changes
nodes.rationale: The system must show the exact AI-proposed mutation and obtain explicit confirmation before committing it.

nodes.label: Server-Side AI Provider Credentials
nodes.rationale: Client UI must not expose credentials or bypass permission-filtered retrieval.

nodes.label: Architect Agent
nodes.rationale: Provides system design, architecture decisions, boundary planning, and tradeoff evaluation before implementation.
nodes.source_location: frontmatter and Use This Agent For

nodes.label: Code Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: Reviews completed changes for defects, regressions, accessibility, maintainability, and missing verification.

nodes.label: Security Reviewer Agent
nodes.rationale: Maps trust boundaries and evaluates exploitable security, privacy, authorization, secret, dependency, and deployment risks.

nodes.label: Test Engineer Agent
nodes.rationale: Designs practical regression coverage and selects the lightest effective verification mix.

nodes.label: App Router Primary Architecture
nodes.source_location: Requirement: Next.js App Router As Primary Architecture

nodes.label: Route Handlers for HTTP Boundaries
nodes.source_location: Requirement: Route Handlers Only For HTTP Boundaries

nodes.label: Browser Evidence Rule
nodes.rationale: Rendered or interactive claims require a real browser when source inspection and automated checks cannot prove visible state.

nodes.label: Next.js App Router Architecture
nodes.rationale: Start with the simplest App Router server architecture and introduce abstraction only when concrete complexity proves the need.

nodes.label: UI Component Discovery
nodes.rationale: Inspect existing project and registry components before creating custom UI to reduce unnecessary bespoke markup and dependency risk.

nodes.label: Seven-document Codebase Contract
nodes.rationale: Repository onboarding is complete only when seven named documents exist, claims are traceable, and unknown or intent-dependent items are marked explicitly.

nodes.label: Server-first Next.js Design
nodes.rationale: Use App Router conventions and introduce server-only data layers or optional abstractions only when protected data or concrete complexity appears.

nodes.label: Private Actionable Feedback
nodes.rationale: Feedback should include useful triage metadata but exclude object bodies, secrets, prompts, exports, and unauthorized identifiers unless explicitly attached.
nodes.source_location: Decision: Feedback must be actionable and private by default

nodes.label: TDD Backpressure
nodes.rationale: Small verified increments constrain implementation scope and expose incorrect assumptions early.

nodes.label: Red Green Refactor
nodes.rationale: Establish a meaningful failing test, make the smallest implementation pass, then improve structure while preserving behavior.

nodes.label: Typed Service Contracts
nodes.rationale: Separate declarative input and output schemas from effectful business logic to create robust type-safe service boundaries.

nodes.label: Agent Human Gates
nodes.rationale: Protected-branch bypasses, merges, production operations, destructive actions, credential and IAM changes, billing, release tags, and protected history changes need explicit authorization.

nodes.label: Main Agent Loop
nodes.rationale: Meaningful work follows discover, OpenSpec routing, focused delegation, implementation, distinct verification streams, risk-proportional review, pull-request handoff, and stop.

nodes.label: Canonical Repository Ownership
nodes.rationale: Each durable concern has one canonical owner, while AGENTS.md and .agents provide vendor-neutral agent configuration and OpenSpec owns durable requirements.

nodes.label: Component Discovery Before Custom UI
nodes.rationale: Inspect project components and registries before creating custom UI, and review third-party source, dependencies, accessibility, compatibility, maintenance, and license.
nodes.source_location: ### Requirement: Component Discovery Before Custom UI

nodes.label: Risk Proportional Verification
nodes.rationale: Completion evidence should match risk and may include lint, types, tests, build, screenshots, browser checks, OpenSpec criteria, or security review; critical workflows justify broader coverage.

nodes.label: Support Feedback and Knowledge Base Proposal
nodes.norm_label: support feedback and knowledge base proposal

nodes.label: Feedback Privacy and Triage Metadata
nodes.rationale: Diagnostic submissions must help triage without transmitting workspace bodies, secrets, prompts, exports, or unauthorized identifiers.
nodes.source_location: ### Requirement: Feedback Privacy and Triage Metadata

nodes.label: Object-First Methodology
nodes.rationale: Teaching connected objects before organization prevents users from recreating folder hierarchies.

nodes.label: Evidence State Parity
nodes.rationale: Appearance and relevant interaction states require same-viewport comparison; software checks, OpenSpec validation, components, or a static screenshot alone do not establish parity.

nodes.label: Live Reference Evidence
nodes.rationale: Measured geometry, computed styles, wording, icons, and interactions from the authenticated reference override remembered behavior and local approximations; unobserved values remain pending.
nodes.source_location: ### Use live reference evidence before local conventions

nodes.label: Capacities Reference Authority
nodes.rationale: A reproducible local difference remains pending until matched or documented as technically infeasible, and unreachable states remain explicitly unverified.

nodes.label: Semantic Intent Classification
nodes.rationale: Threat intent is classified before tool execution as a pre-flight safety check.

nodes.label: Most-restrictive Policy Composition
nodes.rationale: Organization, team, and agent policies combine with deny precedence and intersected allowlists.

nodes.label: Agentic Evaluation Patterns

nodes.label: Evaluator-Optimizer
nodes.rationale: Separating generation and evaluation gives the components clearer responsibilities.

nodes.label: Graph Engineering
nodes.rationale: Dependency graphs expose parallel work and prevent context quality from degrading linearly.

nodes.rationale: An edge exists when one step literally reads another step's output.

nodes.label: Fresh-Context Verification
nodes.rationale: High-stakes claims should be re-derived from source by a context that did not author the synthesis.

nodes.label: Human Approval Gate
nodes.rationale: Verification establishes quality but cannot authorize irreversible or outward-facing action.

nodes.label: Layered Fan-In
nodes.rationale: Consolidating in layers of 20 to 30 preserves specifics and makes completeness auditable.
nodes.source_location: ## Fan-in is where quality is actually lost

nodes.label: Deterministic Full-Path Node IDs
nodes.rationale: Full repo-relative paths prevent same-named entities in different directories from becoming ghost duplicates.

nodes.label: Constrained Graph Vocabulary Expansion
nodes.rationale: Expanding only with vocabulary present in the graph avoids literal-match failures without inventing search tokens.

nodes.label: Replace-on-Re-Extract Merge
nodes.rationale: Changed sources are replaced during merge so stale nodes do not survive incremental updates.

nodes.label: Graph Health Integrity Gate
nodes.rationale: A read-only integrity gate surfaces dangling endpoints, self-loops, and collapsed edges without hiding corruption.

nodes.label: Persistent Knowledge Graph Pipeline
nodes.rationale: A persistent graph makes heterogeneous project content navigable through clustered relationships and auditable evidence.

nodes.label: Verified Spec Sync Before Archive
nodes.rationale: When delta specs are synchronized, verify the resulting main specs before moving the change into the archive.

nodes.label: Artifact Dependency Order
nodes.rationale: Create only the first ready artifact, after reading its completed dependencies, so the schema controls sequence and context.

nodes.label: OPSX Explore Workflow
nodes.rationale: Explore mode is a flexible thinking stance grounded in the codebase; it may capture planning artifacts but must not implement application code.

nodes.label: Workspace Action Contracts
nodes.rationale: Every action needs defined triggers, feedback, state, persistence, cancellation, and failure behavior.
nodes.source_location: ### Treat every action as a contract

nodes.label: Feature-Owned Workspace Styling
nodes.rationale: Workspace-specific tokens and layout behavior belong with the owning feature rather than global CSS.

nodes.label: shadcn-First Composition
nodes.rationale: Existing accessible source primitives should be composed before custom markup is introduced.

nodes.label: Explicit Cross-Space Transfer
nodes.rationale: Copy and move operations must disclose schema, metadata, relation, attachment, permission, and backlink handling.

nodes.label: Spaces as Primary Data Boundary
nodes.rationale: Objects, relations, search, graph, AI retrieval, exports, and sync are space-scoped unless cross-space access is explicitly authorized.
nodes.source_location: ### Spaces are the primary data boundary

nodes.label: OpenSpec Onboarding Cycle
nodes.rationale: Teach the full OpenSpec lifecycle through a small real codebase task using explain, do, show, and pause transitions.

nodes.label: Three-dimensional OpenSpec Verification
nodes.rationale: Assess implementation through completeness, correctness, and coherence with prioritized actionable findings.

nodes.label: Planning-only Boundary
nodes.rationale: Proposal creation authorizes planning artifacts only and requires a new explicit request before implementation.

nodes.label: Software and OpenSpec Verification Separation
nodes.rationale: Software checks prove tooling and application behavior while OpenSpec checks prove agreed requirements; meaningful changes need both.

nodes.label: Measure Before Context Infrastructure
nodes.rationale: Large context is reserve capacity; measure task behavior, accuracy, latency, retries, and token use before adding middleware, indexes, or larger budgets.

nodes.label: Native Search Selection
nodes.rationale: The small repository does not yet justify semantic-index installation overhead; native deterministic search remains sufficient.

nodes.label: CI Deployment Boundary
nodes.rationale: CI success must remain distinct from deployment success until deployment triggers and authentication are configured.

nodes.label: Phased Implementation Order
nodes.rationale: Architecture and evidence guardrails precede shared UI and domain boundaries; AI and portability wait until authorization-aware context is stable.

nodes.label: Stable Document Context
nodes.rationale: Opening contextual tools must preserve the active object's scroll position and editing context.

nodes.label: Harness Drift Checks
nodes.rationale: Repository guidance can silently become stale, so small automated checks should compare instructions with current commands and artifacts.

nodes.label: Failure Memory
nodes.rationale: User-visible, high-risk, or recurring failures should record root cause, prevention, and evidence so they do not recur.

nodes.label: Harness Engineering
nodes.rationale: Repeated coding-agent failures should become durable repository instructions, enforceable checks, failure memory, drift detection, evaluation, and governance.

nodes.label: Component-Level Testing Decision
nodes.rationale: Component tests fit the current app because durable critical flows that justify Playwright do not yet exist.

nodes.label: Verification Engineering Design
nodes.rationale: Objective completion evidence was the highest-value harness improvement; more instructions or tools would add noise.

nodes.label: Main Agent as Loop Controller
nodes.rationale: The main agent should control orchestration while durable state remains in OpenSpec, Git, tests, CI, and pull requests.

nodes.label: Shallow Least-Privilege Delegation
nodes.rationale: Existing specialists should receive minimal read and verification capabilities, with parallel writes deferred unless isolated.

nodes.source_location: Decision: Community links are optional integrations

nodes.norm_label: codex mcp and plugin configuration parity
nodes.rationale: Repository MCP recommendations and user-level plugin or MCP capability should remain aligned without duplicating equivalent integrations.

nodes.label: Trusted Plugin Preference
nodes.community_name: Codex MCP and Plugin Configuration Parity
nodes.rationale: Prefer an official or trusted plugin over raw MCP when it provides equivalent capability, while retaining direct MCP for uncovered needs.

nodes.label: OpenSpec Requirements Lifecycle
nodes.rationale: Durable requirements and rationale belong in OpenSpec changes and canonical specs, with software and spec verification kept separate.

nodes.label: Evidence-backed Codebase Documentation
nodes.rationale: Document only verifiable facts, cite concrete file evidence, mark unknowns TODO, and validate every required section.

nodes.label: Repository Secrets Policy
nodes.rationale: Credentials and production secrets stay out of Git, documentation, OpenSpec, agent configuration, and CI logs.

nodes.label: Editorial Productivity UI
nodes.rationale: Use quiet, dense, content-first workspace UI instead of decorative marketing composition.

nodes.label: CI Verification Alignment
nodes.rationale: Local package-script commands and CI jobs should remain aligned while preserving a stable aggregate Quality context.

nodes.label: Vendor-Neutral Agent Configuration Ownership
nodes.rationale: AGENTS.md and .agents form one portable canonical layer, avoiding duplicated vendor-specific workflow contracts.

nodes.label: Justified Optional Architecture Patterns
nodes.rationale: Ports, repositories, use cases, dependency injection, and composition roots are appropriate only when they provide a concrete testability, provider, workflow, transaction, or wiring benefit.
